case.description: Design a serviceable retention arrangement for a replaceable flat scraper plate in a dry reciprocating test fixture. The plate and moving carriage already exist; the plate must be removed for inspection without disassembling the carriage.
case.valued_outcome: Retain the plate within 1 mm of its initial position over twenty manual strokes, then permit removal and return within sixty seconds without touching its marked working edge.
hard_constraints: Do not drill, cut, heat or glue the plate or carriage.
Keep the marked 30 mm working edge exposed.
No added part may extend into the marked stroke clearance.
The carriage must remain attached to its rails.
resources: One carriage, one 100 by 60 by 2 mm scraper plate and an identical spare plate.
Four 80 mm steel strips, six M4 bolts with nuts, two small magnets, four cork pads and 0.5 m of wire.
Hand drill for strips only, pliers, screwdriver, ruler and marker.
Eighty minutes of fabrication time and twenty minutes of observation.
observations: An unretained plate moves 6 mm after five strokes.
The carriage has two existing mounting slots outside the stroke clearance.
Awkward observation: the spare plate looks identical but the supplied magnets hold it less strongly; in the supplied pull check it releases at 3 N instead of 7 N.

openings.claim: Use bolted strip guides with pivoting retaining straps to capture nonworking plate margins mechanically; release the straps for gloved inspection.
openings.delta: Change the retention dependency from magnetic attraction or pad friction to opposing contact stops carried by the existing mounting slots. Drill strips only; form guides and accessible release tabs with pliers, using cork at contacts. Allocate four strips and the supplied bolts without modifying plate or carriage.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: a magnet-assisted friction clamp. Its available magnetic holding differs between plates; geometric capture should retain either plate despite that difference. Expected distinguishing observation: the spare remains within 1 mm with engaged stops even if magnetic assistance is absent. This is a hypothesis, not demonstrated performance; weaker magnetic pull alone does not predict stroke slip.
openings.probe: First measure slots, plate margins and clearance with ruler; sketch opposing stops and the removal path. Proceed only if supplied strips can be formed and M4 bolts fit without carriage disassembly or forbidden modifications. Fabricate within eighty minutes. In twenty observation minutes, run one configuration three times for twenty strokes, with the spare in the final run. Mark position away from the working edge and measure displacement. Perform three timed removal/return checks, final check wearing supplied thick gloves. Handle nonworking margins only. Require every run within 1 mm and every check within sixty seconds; check returned position too. Observe stop contact, bolt loosening and clearance interference. These establish candidate fitness but do not alone exclude friction as its operating cause.
assumptions: Slot dimensions accept supplied bolts and support the required stop geometry.
Strip thickness permits plier forming and withstands unspecified stroke loads.
Accessible margins permit opposing stops, top restraint and gloved release wholly outside marked clearance.
Defeat conditions include guide flexure, inadequate slot travel, inaccessible fasteners, interference or failed displacement/time limits; resource caps require abandoning an unbuildable candidate.

artifact.assessment: One probe candidate; feasibility remains unresolved because mounting geometry, strip properties and stroke loads are unspecified. No constraint relaxation or deployment claim.

openings.claim: Replace dependence on magnetic holding force with a serviceable mechanical pocket: mounting-slot-supported steel strips contact unmarked plate boundaries, overlapping lips resist lift, and a hinged keeper closes the removal route. Open the keeper and handle an unmarked plate area for inspection.
openings.delta: Change the retention carrier from magnetic attraction to geometric contact. Allocate three strips to fixed boundaries and the fourth to a pivoting keeper, using drilled strip holes, bolts, cork contact pads and a releasable wire latch. The keeper must remain attached during service.
openings.prediction: If the closed pocket has sufficiently small gaps and adequate stiffness, the spare plate stays within 1 mm through twenty strokes despite its weaker magnetic pull. The nearest rival, magnetic retention alone, instead depends on the supplied 3 N versus 7 N difference. Pocket drift should track gap or keeper deformation rather than magnetic pull strength; that relationship remains unmeasured.
openings.probe: First map slots, clearance, exposed edge and removal route with ruler and marker. Proceed only if M4 attachment, strip reach, formability and a gloved unmarked grip fit without modifying the plate or carriage. Use at most two configurations: magnets alone and the pocket. Observe one twenty-stroke run per plate per configuration, with the spare last. Mark initial positions and measure displacement; time one removal/return per plate, using gloves for the spare. Inspect keeper opening and strip deflection. Stay within eighty fabrication and twenty observation minutes and the supplied run/check caps; incomplete timed evidence does not qualify.
assumptions: Slot dimensions, strip stiffness/formability, available overlap outside clearance and safe grip access are unknown.
Defeat conditions include gaps or flex exceeding the displacement allowance, lift escaping the lips, keeper release, or gloved service exceeding sixty seconds.
Magnetic-rival failure is possible, not established; stroke forces are unknown.

artifact.assessment: A proposed probe, not deployment or demonstrated performance. Reject this fabrication if the initial geometry check cannot preserve every hard constraint; do not obtain fit by changing clearance, edge exposure or carriage attachment.

openings.claim: Speculative capability: the weakly magnetic spare could retain its position and support a gloved swap through a mechanically indexed pocket whose opening gate also provides an edge-free handling point.
openings.delta: Change the retention dependency from magnetic attraction or friction to contact boundaries. Bolt drilled steel strips through the existing slots; form side capture and end stops behind the marked edge, with a movable fourth-strip gate. Wire may keep the gate hardware recoverable. Plate pickup must use an accessible unmarked surface; the gate is not assumed to lift it.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: a cork-lined strip clamp using friction alone. If geometric capture supplies retention, the spare should remain within 1 mm even with only light seating pressure, while the friction clamp may drift when its pressure is reduced. Equal success would leave that distinction unresolved; cage drift, trapped extraction, or slow gloved servicing defeats the proposed capability.
openings.probe: First map slots, clearance, exposed edge and unmarked pickup access using ruler and marker. Verify strip bendability, bolt fit and sub-millimetre pocket play before fabrication; abandon if unavailable geometry prevents capture. Within eighty minutes, build at most the pocket and cork-clamp rival using supplied strips, bolts and pads. Within twenty observation minutes, use ruler and stroke counter for up to three twenty-stroke runs per configuration, recording displacement and seating pressure qualitatively. Include the spare in the final twenty-stroke run. Time up to three removal/return checks per configuration with thick gloves, requiring no marked-edge contact and completion within sixty seconds. A pull-scale comparison up to 10 N can characterize escape paths, but cannot establish resistance to unknown stroke forces. Stop early on clearance intrusion or edge-contact necessity.
assumptions: Slot dimensions and locations permit mounting outside stroke clearance.
Strips can be formed with supplied pliers and provide sufficient stiffness.
Available bolts and strips support capture and a gloved gate without modifying plate or carriage.
Stroke duration allows informative comparisons within twenty minutes; otherwise fewer runs reduce confidence.

artifact.assessment: Bounded enabling experiment, not deployment. Feasibility remains uncertain until mounting, capture and pickup geometry are checked. Reduced magnetic dependence addresses the supplied anomaly but does not prove retention or serviceability.
